key_insight: An arbitrary-order Discrete de Rham scheme combines augmented Lagrangian contact enforcement with fracture-face enrichment to achieve optimal convergence for displacement and contact multipliers.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of contact and friction between fracture walls in linearly elastic media on polytopal meshes.
method: Recast normal contact constraints and Tresca friction as projection identities in a unified augmented Lagrangian formulation.
Discretise displacement with arbitrary-degree DDR spaces, enriched by fracture-face bubble degrees of freedom.
Establish stability through a discrete lifting and derive an abstract optimal-order error estimate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive numerical experiments confirming the convergence analysis and demonstrating practical accuracy and robustness, without specifying quantitative results.
watch_item: Fracture-face bubble enrichment is essential to the stability argument and adds implementation complexity.
paper_title: An Arbitrary-Order Augmented Lagrangian Discrete De Rham Scheme for Contact Mechanics with Tresca Friction
